chunks: Ibn Mahbub from Abu Waddad said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a sick man who confessed at the time of death to an heir that he owed him a debt. He said: That is permissible. I said: And if he bequeathed something to an heir? He said: It is permissible.

key_terms.إِقْرَار: Confession or acknowledgment of a debt or right
key_terms.عِندَ الْمَوْتِ: At the time of death / in the hour of death

ai.seo_question: Is a dying person's confession of debt to an heir legally valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a dying person’s acknowledgment of debt to an heir is legally valid, ensuring the debt is settled from the estate before distribution. He further confirms that bequeathing specific assets to an heir is permissible, resolving the scholarly debate on whether an heir can receive both their fixed inheritance share and additional bequests without conflict. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding estate settlement and the rights of heirs to hold multiple claims against the deceased's estate.
